title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-priya-wip-4
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent drop in metrics and traces (~5-15% traffic windows) observed since 2026-02-10. Logs ingestion partially unaffected but traces show large gaps (many services missing spans for 30s windows).
- Hypothesis: buffer/backpressure in otel-collector or exporter throttling. Also possible header propagation break in tracing-proxy after rollout on 2026-02-09.

Observed symptoms (high level):
- Dashboard: per-route trace counts drop to ~0 for 10-30s, then resume. Metrics ingest shows corresponding small deltas and NaN spikes on aggregated counters.
- Error surfaces: otel-collector logs show repeated `exporter temporarily unavailable` messages and `queue_retry` attempts. K8s metrics for CPU/memory stable; no node OOM.
- Some services report 500s from obs-ingest when upstream batching backlog increases.

Breadcrumbs / commands I ran (chronological):
1) Quick check of pods (10:12):
- kubectl -n observability get pods -o wide | grep obs-ingest
  -> obs-ingest-5d7c9f (READY 2/2) obs-otel-collector-72f (READY 1/1)

2) Tail collector logs around incident window (10:14 - 10:18):
- kubectl -n observability logs -f obs-otel-collector-72f --since=20m | grep -i exporter
  Found repeated: `2026-02-25T10:15:03Z WARN exporter/http: failed to send batch: 503 Service Unavailable`
  Also: `queue_processor.go: queue_retry: drop_count=12`

3) Check obs-ingest pod logs (10:20):
- kubectl -n observability logs obs-ingest-5d7c9f -c ingest --since=30m | sed -n '1,200p'
  -> intermittent `context deadline exceeded` for downstream calls to storage-writer. Latency climbing from 120ms -> 1.8s during windows.

4) Verify exporter endpoints health (10:25):
- curl -v http://metrics-exporter.internal/health
  -> 200 OK most times, but at 10:15 returned 503 once. Logs on metrics-exporter show keepalive failures to backend (cloud-monitoring).

5) Trace propagation check (10:35):
- Made a synthetic request through tracing-proxy and GREP for trace-id across services:
  export TRACE_ID=$(mktemp); curl -sS -H "x-trace-id: test-123" https://gateway.local/health-check -o /dev/null
  kubectl -n svc logs gateway --since=1m | grep test-123 -> present
  kubectl -n svc logs service-a --since=1m | grep test-123 -> MISSING
  -> indicates trace header lost between gateway and service-a; tracing-proxy rollout 2026-02-09 might be related.

6) Check proxy config and envoy filters (10:40):
- kubectl -n proxies get configmap tracing-proxy-config -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
  -> saw sampling.enabled=false (ouch) for some routes; also noticed header rewrite rules.

Immediate errors/snippets collected:
- otel-collector: `WARN exporter/http: failed to send batch: 503 Service Unavailable`
- otel-collector: `WARN queue_processor: retrying batch, attempt=3`
- obs-ingest: `error: context deadline exceeded (rpc to storage-writer)`
- tracing-proxy: `INFO header_rewrite: removed x-trace-id for route /internal`
- metrics-aggregator: `panic: NaN encountered in counter aggregator; resetting` (transient)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Exporter/backpressure: otel-collector exporter to cloud-monitoring intermittently returns 503, collector queue backs up and starts dropping batches which results in missing traces and NaN metrics. This matches collector warnings and exporter 503 seen in logs.
2) Header propagation break: tracing-proxy config change removed x-trace-id for internal routes, causing spans to be created without parent ids and thus not stitched - explains some missing spans but not all.
3) Upstream storage-writer latency: obs-ingest timeouts to storage-writer cause partial ingestion failures and backpressure to collector.
4) Resource saturation at exporter backend (cloud-monitoring) in specific AZ/region resulting in 503s.

Tests to validate hypotheses (done/in-progress):
- Reproduced header propagation loss with synthetic request -> confirmed header rewrite removing x-trace-id. (validates hypothesis #2)
- Temporarily configured otel-collector to use a local noop-exporter to see if trace counts stabilize (A/B test):
  * change configmap to route traces to local no-op and roll collector -> trace counts remain stable during a 10m window. Suggests exporter/backpressure is causal. (validates #1)
- Increased collector queue size/timeout in staging and ran load test -> reduced drop rate but some drops persisted.
- Contacted storage-writer team for latency logs (ticket OBS-4123). They reported GC spikes around the same windows. (supports #3)

Config diffs of interest (notes):
- tracing-proxy v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 rolled 2026-02-09 added header_rewrite rules; default sampling config changed. Need small patch to preserve x-trace-id on internal headers.
- otel-collector config: exporter retry_policy: initial_interval 5s, max_interval 60s; queue settings: num_consumers=2, queue_size=512. We saw queue_drop_count increase; suggested temporary increase queue_size -> 2048 for next trial.

Quick mitigation attempted (2026-02-18):
- Rolled back tracing-proxy header rewrite for internal routes -> immediate improvement in span continuity for service-a and service-b.
- Switched collector to buffering mode and increased queue_size -> reduced dropped count but exporter still reported occasional 503.
- Turned on rate-limited sampling on high-volume endpoints to reduce traffic to exporter as short-term relief.

Open action items / next steps:
- [ ] Work with storage-writer team to reduce GC pauses or increase write parallelism (OBS-4123) - Ethan to follow up for timeline.
- [ ] Patch tracing-proxy (small hotfix) to preserve tracing headers; include backwards-compatible test. (assigned Amelia)
- [ ] Investigate long-term solution for exporter 503s: scale exporter horizontally or use regional failover. Confirm cloud-monitoring SLA and quotas. (Priya)
- [ ] Add more granular telemetry inside collector export pipeline (per-exporter queue depth metric) and alert on drop_count > 0 for > 30s.
- [ ] Postmortem draft if incident repeats: capture timeline, config diffs, and mitigation steps.

Notes for postmortem (raw):
- Root cause likely multi-factor: header rewrite increased apparent missing spans (operational/visibility issue) + persistent exporter/backpressure and storage-writer latency causing real ingestion loss.
- Short-term: header hotfix + increase buffering + sampling reductions.
- Medium-term: exporter scaling/HA + persistent queue depth metrics and alerting + improve storage writer throughput.

Misc scratch commands and helpful snippets:
- Check otel-collector queue metrics:
  kubectl -n observability exec -it obs-otel-collector-72f -- curl localhost:8888/metrics | grep exporter_queue_drop_count

- Find pods with highest restart counts (maybe crash loops):
  kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide

- Quick trace header test:
  curl -v -H "x-trace-id: debug-$(date +%s)" https://gateway.local/endpoint &&
  kubectl -n svc logs --since=2m | grep debug-<ts> (replace <ts> accordingly)

Notes to self: keep this doc updated as we try changes in staging before prod. Save config diffs in PR with clear rollbacks. Capture timestamps for each test so we can correlate with exporter/cloud-monitoring logs.

References and links: JIRA OBS-4123 (storage-writer), PR #278 (obs-ingest buffering tweaks), Confluence architecture page for pipeline.

-- Priya
